findings.heading: Install Git / Installer Git
findings.proposition: English states installing Git from git-scm.com is a mandatory first step ("You must first install Git"); the French states it as an option ("Vous pouvez d'abord installer Git").
findings.reader_consequence: A French reader treats installing Git as optional, skips it, and then finds that RStudio and Github Desktop have no Git engine to drive, with no instruction telling them the install was required.

findings.heading: Process overview / Aperçu du processus
findings.proposition: English says step 5 merges the online working branch into the online "main" branch in order to transfer the changes; the French says the merge is done "afin de créer une nouvelle branche" (in order to create a new branch).
findings.reader_consequence: A French reader is told the purpose of merging is to create a branch, which is false, and never learns that the merge is what moves their work into main.

findings.heading: Process overview / Aperçu du processus
findings.proposition: English says the branch formerly called "master" is now called "main"; the French says it is now called "principale" glossed as ("master"), giving "master" as the current name.
findings.reader_consequence: A French reader concludes the current default branch name is still master, so they will not recognise or look for the "main" branch that Github creates by default and that the rest of the chapter refers to.

findings.heading: Pull and push changes up to Github / Tirez et poussez les modifications vers Github
findings.proposition: English glosses "committed but not pushed" as "(i.e. are still local)"; the French glosses it as "(c'est-à-dire qu'elles sont toujours en cours de traitement)" — still being processed.
findings.reader_consequence: A French reader loses the definition that unpushed commits exist only on their own machine, which is the exact fact that makes those commits easy to revert.

findings.heading: In Rstudio (pull/push) / Dans Rstudio
findings.proposition: English gives the command `git config --global user.email "..."`; the French translates the configuration key and gives `git config --global utilisateur.email "..."`.
findings.reader_consequence: A French reader typing the command gets a Git error, because `utilisateur.email` is not a Git configuration key; the very next bullet keeps `user.name` untranslated, so they have no way to infer the correct key.

findings.heading: In Github Desktop (delete branch) / Dans Github
findings.proposition: English instructs the reader to check out (switch to) the branch to be deleted and then use Branch > Delete; the French instructs them to "vérifier" (check) that the branch appears in the Branch > Delete menu, and drops the checkout step.
findings.reader_consequence: A French reader never switches to the target branch, and Github Desktop's Branch > Delete acts on the currently checked-out branch, so they delete the wrong branch.

findings.heading: This sounds complicated, I am not a programmer / Cela semble compliqué, je ne suis pas un programmeur
findings.proposition: English advises: if you are NOT on a project where collaborating through Git is a necessity, it is a good time to get confident with it solo. The French inserts a second negation ("un projet où la collaboration ... n'est pas une nécessité"), inverting the condition so the advice applies to readers who DO need Git collaboration.
findings.reader_consequence: A French reader who works alone reads the advice as not addressed to them and postpones learning Git, which is the opposite of the recommendation.

findings.heading: Install an interface (optional but recommended) / Installer une interface
findings.proposition: English states you can use the console occasionally for an action your interface does not support; the French note omits this.
findings.reader_consequence: A French reader who hits an action their client cannot perform does not learn that dropping to the console for that one action is a normal, supported option, and may believe they must switch clients.

findings.heading: Install an interface (optional but recommended) / Installer une interface
findings.proposition: English states you can also perform any number of actions online on Github itself; the French note omits this.
findings.reader_consequence: A French reader does not learn that the Github website is itself a usable interface for Git actions, so they will not use it when their local client is unavailable.

findings.heading: Vocabulary, concepts and basic functions / Vocabulaire, concepts et fonctions de base
findings.proposition: English states that it is good to have the vocabulary and concepts in mind in order to build a mental model, and that they are needed when using interfaces anyway; the French sentence stops after "nous montrerons comment utiliser les interfaces".
findings.reader_consequence: A French reader is given no reason to learn the vocabulary section that follows and may skip straight to the interface instructions, then meet untranslated terms (commit, stage, remote) with no mental model.

findings.heading: Commits
findings.proposition: English's staging example has two pieces of work — model specification in one script AND later a figure in another script; the French drops "and later on a figure in", leaving only a model in "un autre script".
findings.reader_consequence: The French example no longer shows two distinct pieces of work, so the case for two separate commits collapses, and the parenthetical that follows refers to reverting "les changements sur la figure" — a figure the French text never mentioned.

findings.heading: In Github Desktop (commit) / Dans le bureau de Github
findings.proposition: English says you give the commit a name and OPTIONALLY a description; the French lists the description with no marker of optionality ("donnez un nom à la livraison, une description, puis cliquez").
findings.reader_consequence: A French reader believes a description is required for every commit in Github Desktop and spends effort writing one, or hesitates to commit without it.

findings.heading: Pull and push changes up to Github / Tirez et poussez les modifications vers Github
findings.proposition: English concludes the note with the recommendation to push only once you are done introducing the changes for the task you were working on; the French note ends at the parenthetical and omits this recommendation.
findings.reader_consequence: A French reader gets the comparison of revert difficulty but not the actionable rule it supports, so they do not learn when to push.

findings.heading: In Github: submitting pull requests / Dans Github : soumettre des demandes de pull
findings.proposition: English says a pull request can be submitted from the website OR from Github Desktop; the French says "à partir du site Web ... ou à partir de Github", dropping "Desktop" so both alternatives name the same place.
findings.reader_consequence: A French Github Desktop user does not learn they can open a pull request from the application and assumes they must go to the website.
